Core Web Vitals metrics (LCP, FID, CLS), WordPress speed optimization workflows, HTTP security headers context, and advanced Claude Code usage patterns. High signal-to-noise content with actionable optimization tactics and numbered hacks.
operating_rules: First Input Delay must be under 100ms; 300ms+ becomes bad
Largest Contentful Paint should occur within 2.5 seconds
Cumulative Layout Shift score should not exceed 0.1 (10% max viewport shift)
Google recommends TTFB under 200ms
FCP target: under 1.8 seconds
TTI (Time to Interactive) target: under 3.8 seconds
Page speed matters for conversion: 100ms delay = 1% sales drop (Amazon study); 3+ second load = 53% mobile user abandonment (Google); 1 second improvement = 2% conversion lift (Walmart)
Preload only critical resources necessary for above-the-fold rendering
Lazy load non-critical images and below-the-fold content
Disable emoji libraries if not used (saves server resources)
Heartbeat API should be turned on to save server resources
Use AVIF/WebP formats for images (AVIF better compression, WebP broader support)
Minify HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Combine CSS and JS files to reduce HTTP requests
Enable browser caching with long TTL for static assets, short/no cache for frequently updated content
CDN cache hit ratio target: 95-99% for mostly static content
For WordPress: turn off lazy load images in Breeze if it delays first image load (counterproductive)
Varnish cache should be set to auto-purge
DNS lookups add latency; apply DNS prefetching only to critical resources
Gzip/Brotli compression: use Brotli as primary with Gzip fallback
Layout thrashing (reading then writing DOM in same iteration) forces repeated recalculations; separate read and write operations
GPU animations (transform, opacity) better than CPU animations (width, height, margin)
Web Workers for heavy computation; never use for simple operations
Request animation frame for chunked task execution to prevent main thread blocking
Use Intersection Observer for smart lazy loading; avoid simple threshold-based conditions
Claude Code: exit early and reprompt when going wrong direction (saves context)
Claude Code: challenge outputs aggressively; push for second attempt when ok is not good enough
Claude Code: run parallel sessions with git worktrees for multi-branch development
gates: Mobile device performance must match desktop (not assume mobile users will tolerate slower loads)
E-commerce sites: prioritize loading speed above UI speed (conversion dependency)
B2B/SaaS apps: prioritize UI speed above loading speed (session length and workflow matter)
Task-oriented apps (Figma, Google Sheets): UI speed critical; long sessions amplify slowness impact
Image optimization gate: never lazy load above-the-fold images
CSS animations gate: only animate transform and opacity properties on composition layer
Layout shift gate: avoid animations that trigger reflows (width, height, padding, margin)
Content Security Policy must be validated for actual attack surface, not just best-practice compliance
X-Frame-Options header only critical if site has sensitive functionality that could be clickjacked
prompts: Using PageSpeed Insights (page speed.web.dev): paste URL, click analyze, review mobile performance first
Screenshot analysis loop for design: design, screenshot, analyze visually, implement, repeat 3 times before V1
Query DNS prefetching for critical resources only (fonts, stylesheets, critical scripts)
Lazy load decision framework: will images be off-screen initially? Can users reach them through scrolling?
Cache decision framework: is this content public (cache yes), dynamic (short TTL), or private (never cache)?
Performance bottleneck diagnosis: TTFB issue = server/network, FCP issue = rendering blockage, LCP issue = asset size/load order, CLS issue = layout calculations
